value.title: Conditional Theorem 9 specialization and receiver marginalization
value.summary: Premise-bounded specialization of the cited Gohari--Liu--Nair Theorem 9 system to private messages, including the exact 30-row expansion, input-only product-marginal reduction, conditional capacity-bound formulation, Q0-supported local-value foundations, exact finite-grid at-most-N-output reductions, the exact Q0 receiver infimum and necessary midpoint coercivity, and a continuous weak-duality upper certificate for one fixed binary auxiliary-receiver pair.

value.title: Finite-grid receiver reduction and exact Q0 foundations
value.summary:
Using the accepted private-message 30-row definitions and optimization order of transaction e3c1036ca607539a5ebcddf3058e6014ac5c1cd9, let Q be any N-point posterior grid containing {0,1/2,1}. Every finite-output binary-input receiver has an at-most-N-output replacement with the same mutual-information samples on Q, so inf_{G,K finite} V_Q(G,K) = inf_{|G|,|K|<=N} V_Q(G,K); when Q is reflection closed, inf_{m finite} V_Q(m,m^circ) = inf_{|supp(m)|<=N} V_Q(m,m^circ). For Q0={0,1/2,1} and c=h_2(1/4)-1/2, inf_{G,K finite} V_{Q0}(G,K) = inf_{m finite} V_{Q0}(m,m^circ) = c. Moreover, for every finite-output input-only pair G,K with g=J_G(1/2), k=J_K(1/2), B(G,K) >= V_0(g,k) >= max{F(g),F(k)}, where F(x)=2c max{c,x}/(c+x); consequently, if c <= U < 2c and B(G,K) <= U, then 2c^2/U-c <= g,k <= Uc/(2c-U). These are finite-grid and necessary-coercivity statements only, with no continuum cardinality, limit interchange, or full-functional reflected-optimality assertion.

Scope qualifications:
- The result is limited to finite posterior grids and finite-output receivers.
- The reflected-class conclusion is proved only for reflection-closed finite grids; no full-functional reflected-optimality assertion is established.
- No continuum cardinality theorem, attainment claim, limit interchange, capacity-converse interpretation, or improved sum-capacity bound is established.
- The declared reference is needed for the accepted 30-row definitions, optimization order, single-output term structure, and the inequality V_Q(G,K) <= B(G,K); external manuscript authenticity is not required.

value.title: Proof of the finite-grid reduction and Q0 coercivity foundations
value.summary: Proof record bounded to `root/result/finite-grid-q0-foundations`. It represents each finite-output binary-input receiver by its fair-prior posterior measure and expresses its sampled mutual-information curve as integrals of continuous functions. Caratheodory's convex-hull theorem then preserves the posterior mean and all samples on an N-point grid using at most N outputs; posterior mutual-information identities and the accepted single-output audit transfer this equality to every receiver term in the Q-supported 30-row system. For Q0, the proof parametrizes each hierarchy block by three scalars, establishes the row symmetry, and verifies the H, L, and X witness families covering all midpoint pairs to obtain the accepted coercive floor. A reflection-invariant three-output revealing-erasure receiver and one accepted sum row give the matching Q0 upper construction. Solving the two branches of the accepted scalar floor yields the stated necessary midpoint window. The proof establishes only the finite-grid and necessary-coercivity claim and does not establish continuum cardinality, limit interchange, full-functional reflected optimality, or an improved capacity bound.

value.title: Exact symbolic audit for the finite-grid Q0 foundations
value.summary: A Python standard-library symbolic checker associated only with the accepted finite-grid Q0 result. It requires the sole logical dependency transaction, independently rebuilds the 30 private-message rows and compares their normalized signature with the reviewed dependency signature, checks the receiver-skew row symmetry, verifies all H, L, and X row and block slacks by exact coefficientwise polynomial nonnegativity, and checks the common-curve upper construction algebraically. It uses no floating-point arithmetic, optimizer, third-party package, or network request. The checker is corroborative tooling: it does not re-prove Caratheodory's theorem, supply a continuum cardinality argument, or constitute an independent objective execution attestation or mathematical claim.
